rulings.evidence: Follows the 2026-08-27 'bone broth' ruling and refuses the board's chicken-broth bridge for the same reason: bone broth is a 6-8 dollar quart against a 1.50-2.50 carton and carries 10 g protein per cup against 1. Same-form vocabulary row exists.

The DIFFERENT FORM 'mix' flag is a wording artefact - the vocabulary's own name is Ranch Seasoning Mix and this line is a packet of exactly that. Board 6 of 7, cheapest 0.53 at Walmart. One packet is 28 g.
Bare 'cayenne' is ground cayenne pepper; the FDC shelf returns only 'Spices, pepper, red or cayenne'. REUSE of a live board id at 6 of 7, and the DB already carries the row.
The sweet/whole/canned form flags are spurious - the line IS a can, exactly the 2026-08-26 'chopped green chiles' call. Board has no commodity but today's captures carry it, so the term is enqueued.

Fire-roasted is a label variant of the same diced can at the same shelf price, the 'reduced sodium beef broth' -> beef-broth call. Deliberately REFUSED the board's `tomatoes` match, which is the fresh field tomato - a wrong-food match at a wrong price.

rulings.raw: 15 oz can dark red kidney beans
rulings.evidence: Same-form vocabulary row and a live board id at 7 of 7, cheapest 0.0548 at Aldi; dark versus light red is a shade of the same canned bean at one price. Drained yield of a 15 oz can.
The 'canned' form flag is spurious - the line is a 4 oz can, and the 2026-08-26 ruling on this exact situation went here. Board 6 of 7. The dried guajillo and arbol rows are a different food.

'Cooked' is a prep instruction, not a form flip - you buy raw bacon and fry it. Board 7 of 7. Weighed on the cooked basis (10 crisp slices, about 100 g) because the rendered fat is discarded rather than added to the chili.

REUSE of shredded-cheese, live at 7 of 7 and cheapest 0.1521 at Sam's Club: a Mexican blend is the same bagged shred at the same price class. Refused ricotta/provolone/Boursin, which are different cheeses entirely.
